keyframe_review.note: 3.94 M km2 for 1294-1304; infobox 'about 3,750,000 km2 ... estimated for 1310' (ratio 0.95 with this shape, 0.99 with the 1305 shape). The shape runs from the Aegean side of Anatolia (27.6 E) to Sind and from the Caucasus to the Gulf of Oman. The Ghazan page has Anatolia under a Mongol viceroy (Taghachar, reappointed 10 November 1295) and the Rum Seljuk sultan Mesud II 'arrested and jailed in Hamadan', so the Anatolian part is Ilkhanid-administered; Cliopatria's west-Anatolian step in 1305 is handled in the ledger.

3.71 M km2 for 1305-1313 against the infobox's 3.75 M for 1310 (ratio 0.99). 824 cells of west and central Anatolia (27.6-37.9 E) leave the shape and appear as Cliopatria's Sultanate of Rum (255 cells), Hamid (155), Kastamonu (72), Karaman (70), Sinop (50) and the Eshrefids (48). The pages do not say the Ilkhanate lost them: the Rum page has the sultanate 'officially subject' to the Mongols from 1256 with Mesud II sultan to 1308, and the Abu Said page has Ilkhanid governors of Anatolia (Timurtash after 1319, Hasan reinstated 1332). The ledger therefore records a loss of direct control in 1305 followed by a vassal tint, not a loss to independent states. East of Anatolia the shape stands.
3.71 M km2 for 1314-1332; five cells different from 1305 on the Sind edge (the Khalji frontier), no event on the pages. Infobox 3.75 M for 1310 (ratio 0.99).

3.58 M km2 for 1333-1343: 523 cells in the Caucasus (40.9-47.4 E, 38.9-42.8 N) pass to Cliopatria's Kingdom of Georgia, which the Ilkhanate page ties to 1330 ('Abkhazia annexed, reunifying Georgia'); Georgia kept paying tribute ('1336-1350: Georgian tribute fell by about three-quarters'), so the ledger adds a vassal tint. Years: the page ends the independent khanate with Abu Said's death on 30 November 1335 and lists puppet Ilkhans to 1357; Cliopatria keeps one Ilkhanate shape to 1343 and starts the Jalayirids, Muzaffarids, Sarbadars, Kartids, Chobanids and Injuids in 1344. For 1336-1343 the shape is a nominal Ilkhanate over fragmenting emirates (unverified: page budget).

ledger.note: 1294: the Ilkhanate appears on Cliopatria's map when its Mongol Empire row ends in 1293 (the mongol-empire dossier lists it as a successor from 1294). The page's own dates are older: 'In 1258 the Abbasid Caliphate was destroyed, and Hulegu proclaimed himself ilkhan'; infobox 'Independent khanate (1260-1335)'.

ledger.note: 1343: the Ilkhanate is replaced by its successors on Cliopatria's map (they start in 1344). The pages put the real end earlier and later: the Ilkhanate page's infobox ends the independent khanate in 1335, the Abu Said page says he 'died without an heir or appointed successor. Clashes followed among major families' and the Ilkhanate 'became a set of small kingdoms'; the Ilkhanate page lists puppet Ilkhans to 1357 (Anushirwan 1343-1356, Ghazan II 1356-1357) and has 'Little' Hasan take Azerbaijan in 1338 and Jani Beg of the Golden Horde take Tabriz in 1357. The Abu Said page names the Chupanids, Jalayirids, Sarbadars and Muzaffarids as the successor states.

wars.name: Ilkhanate-Chagatai war of Duwa and Qutlugh Khwaja
wars.outcome: Duwa invades Khorasan on 9 December 1295; Ghazan musters about 80,000 troops against Chagatai raiders under Qutlugh Khwaja in 1303; the war ends in the 'general peace among the Mongol khanates' of 1304.

wars.name: Mongol invasions of Syria under Ghazan
wars.outcome: Ghazan takes Aleppo (October 1299), wins at Wadi al-Khazandar (23/24 December 1299), holds Damascus for days (30 December 1299 to 6 January 1300, citadel unbroken), raids again in February 1301 and is defeated at Marj al-Saffar in April 1303. No land is kept; peace follows in 1322.
wars.note: Ilkhanate page: Abu Said concluded a peace treaty with the Mamluks in 1322.

wars.name: Rebellion of Sulemish in Anatolia
wars.outcome: Sulemish's revolt ends in defeat near Erzincan on 27 April 1299; he is burned at Tabriz on 27 September 1299. No land changes.

wars.name: Revolt of the emirs against Abu Said
belligerents: rebel emirs (Irenchin) and the Chagatayid Yasa'ur
wars.outcome: Irenchin's rebellion is crushed at Zanjan-Rud on 13 July 1319 (Ilkhanate page) and the rebel emirs near Mianeh on 20 June 1319 (Abu Said page); Georgia's governor Qurumishi is executed; the Chagatayid Yasa'ur revolts in 1319 and is killed by Kebek in 1320. No land changes.
wars.note: The Ilkhanate page dates the Zanjan-Rud battle '13 July 1319' and Chupan's pilgrimage 1325; the Abu Said page dates Hamadani's execution near Abhar 13 July 1318.

wars.name: Golden Horde invasions of Azerbaijan
wars.outcome: Oz Beg invades Azerbaijan in 1319 with the Chagatayid Yasa'ur, again in the mid-1320s against Chupan and in 1335, when Abu Said dies on the way to meet him in Karabakh. No land changes.
wars.note: The Ilkhanate page lists Golden Horde invasions in 1318, 1324 and 1335.

wars.name: Collapse of the Ilkhanate
wars.outcome: After Abu Said's death the Hulaguid line continues under puppet Ilkhans (Arpa Ke'un 1335-1336, Musa 1336-1337, Muhammad 1336-1338, Sati Beg 1338-1339, Sulayman 1339-1343) while the emirs divide the land; 'Little' Hasan takes Azerbaijan in 1338.
wars.note: Successor shapes in Cliopatria start in 1344.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line on the pages opened: the Mamluk frontier on the Euphrates was fixed by war, and the 1322 peace gives no line; the Caucasus, Khorasan and Anatolian frontiers are approximate.

notes:
Dates. Cliopatria's Ilkhanate starts in 1294 and ends in 1343; the pages give 1256-1259 (province of the Mongol Empire), 1260 (independent khanate, infobox) and 1335 (Abu Said's death), with puppet Ilkhans to 1357. This dossier keeps 1294-1343 because it must match the mongol-empire dossier (which ends in 1293) and the successor rows (which start in 1344); the older phase (Hulegu 1256/1258-1293, Maragheh and Tabriz capitals, Berke's war of 1262) is not drawn separately.

Anatolia. Cliopatria's 1305 step removes 824 cells of west and central Anatolia; the pages opened do not date a retreat (the Rum page, the beyliks page and the Abu Said page keep Mongol suzerainty and Ilkhanid governors to 1332), so the ledger writes a loss of direct control (confidence 1) and a vassal tint, with 10 events at confidence 1 that a gap-filler could replace with a page on the Ilkhanid governors of Rum (Timurtash, Eretna). The Sultanate of Rum row (1305-1313) is a vassal of the Ilkhans; its end in 1308 is the murder of Mesud II (infobox: Karamanid conquest 1308, body: 1328). Trebizond (vassal from 1243 on the Ilkhanate page) and the Armenian Kingdom of Cilicia (King Hethum II joined Ghazan at Aleppo in 1299) were also vassals but no page opened dates their end, so no vassal pair is written for them.

Georgia. The Caucasus step of 1333 (523 cells) is Cliopatria's; the page ties it to 1330 and keeps Georgia tributary. The Ilkhanate 1294-1332 shape includes Georgia as directly held land, which the pages describe as a Mongol-conquered tributary kingdom with Ilkhanid governors.

Disagreements: Ilkhanate page dates Irenchin's defeat at Zanjan-Rud 13 July 1319, the Abu Said page the defeat of the emirs near Mianeh 20 June 1319 and Hamadani's execution 13 July 1318; Golden Horde invasions in 1318/1319, 1324 and 1335.

Successors: Jalayirids, Chobanids, Muzaffarids, Sarbadars, Kartids and Injuids are Cliopatria rows (other groups write them: the Abu Said page names Chupanids, Jalayirids, Sarbadars, Muzaffarids). Not written anywhere: the Qara'unas (Khorasan) and the Eretnids of Sivas (1335, beyliks page); a gap-filler should add Eretna as a counterpart of the Anatolian events. The Golden Horde events of 1356-1357 (Tabriz) have this dossier's counterpart on the Ilkhanate side only in the Hulaguid puppet line (Ghazan II 1356-1357); the golden-horde dossier carries them.

Gazetteer: every name used resolves (Khorasan region, Syria country, Cliopatria shapes). Page budget: five pages of five (Ilkhanate, Ghazan, Abu Said, Anatolian beyliks, Sultanate of Rum).
